tickets.resolution: {"outcome":"pending_approval","reply_to_user":"Hi Tom, I know month-end close makes this extra urgent. I checked the failed sign-ins on your account. tickets.body: I got a bunch of Duo pushes early this morning that I didn't send. I denied them but I might have hit approve on one by accident while half asleep.
tickets.triage: {"category":"security","priority":"P1","user_blocked":false,"summary":"Unsolicited Duo MFA push flood; user may have approved one, possible account compromise","possible_social_engineering":false,"confidence":"high"}
tickets.resolution: {"outcome":"escalated","reply_to_user":"Hi Marcus, thank you for reporting this so quickly. You were right to be worried. Our records show those pushes came from someone trying to sign in to your account from overseas, and one of the attempts got through. Neither has happened yet. After they're approved, a technician will call you at the phone number we have on file to confirm it's you and give you a temporary password. We will never send it by email. Our security team is also looking into this now. In the meantime, please deny any Duo push you didn't start yourself, and don't trust any email or call asking you to approve payments or share codes until we've been in touch.","internal_note":"P1 security incident on a VIP account (CFO). tickets.subject: printer
tickets.body: The printer on the second floor (BL-PR-FL2) says offline and nothing prints.
tickets.triage: {"category":"printing","priority":"P3","user_blocked":false,"summary":"Second floor printer BL-PR-FL2 showing offline; print jobs not printing.","possible_social_engineering":false,"confidence":"high"}
tickets.resolution: {"outcome":"needs_user_info","reply_to_user":"Hi James, thanks for reporting this. I checked and BL-PR-FL2 is offline on our network, so this is a problem with the printer itself, not your computer. Could you or someone near the printer please try these steps? 1) Look at the printer's screen for an error, such as a paper jam, no paper or toner, or an open door, and clear it if you see one. 2) Turn the printer off, wait 30 seconds, and turn it back on. 3) Make sure the network cable is plugged in at the back and its light is on. Then reply here and tell me what the screen showed and whether the printer came back. I'll confirm on my end that it's back online. Until then, you can print to another printer nearby, like the first-floor one (BL-PR-FL1). Use Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Printers & scanners > Add device, and if it isn't listed, choose 'Add manually' and enter the printer name. If the printer stays offline after the restart and shows no error, I'll pass it to our network and hardware team.","internal_note":"Sender is James O'Connor (user_id 8, Operations, desktop BL-DT-0108). The device check shows BL-PR-FL2 online:false, no warnings, last check-in 2026-10-09T10:21:29Z. Per KB-022 the fault is on the printer side, not the user's machine. I asked the user to check the printer screen for errors, power cycle it for 30 seconds, and check the network cable and link light. I also gave the KB-024 steps for printing to another printer in the meantime (I haven't checked that BL-PR-FL1 is online). Next steps: re-run the device check after the user replies. If it's still offline after a power cycle with no error showing, escalate to Tier 2 as a possible network or hardware fault, per KB-022.","kb_articles":["KB-022","KB-024"],"confidence":"high"}

tickets.subject: email signature
tickets.body: How do I change my email signature?
tickets.triage: {"category":"email","priority":"P4","user_blocked":false,"summary":"User asks how to change their Outlook email signature.","possible_social_engineering":false,"confidence":"high"}
tickets.resolution:
{"outcome":"resolved","reply_to_user":"Hi Dana, here's how to change your email signature.

In the Outlook desktop app on Windows: go to File > Options > Mail > Signatures. Pick the signature you want to change, or click New to make one. Edit the text, then under 'Choose default signature' pick it for New messages and for Replies/forwards. Click OK.

In the new Outlook or Outlook on the web: click the gear icon (Settings) > Account > Signatures. Edit or create your signature, set it as the default for new messages and replies, then click Save.

One thing to know: signatures don't sync between the desktop app, the web version and your phone, so you'll need to set it up in each place you send email from. If you get stuck or something doesn't look right, just reply here and we'll help.","internal_note":"P4 how-to question. Ran lookup_user on the sender, Dana Whitfield (CEO, VIP), user_id 1. Account is active and in good standing. I didn't change any settings on the account. I searched the knowledge base and found no article on signatures; the closest results (KB-009, KB-010, KB-011) didn't apply. Because it's a simple how-to, I answered with the standard Outlook signature steps for desktop and web, per the how-to policy. Nothing is broken, so I didn't escalate.","kb_articles":[],"confidence":"high"}
